title: Slow English Podcast #373: 20 Easy Facts About Burundi

sentences.text: you are here today. Today we will learn about a beautiful country in East Africa. The country
is Burundi. I will speak slowly and use easy English. Let's begin.
Fact one, Burundi is in Africa. Burundi is a small country in East Africa. It is next to
Rwanda, Tanzania and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Burundi is a landlocked country.
This means it does not have a sea or ocean coast. The country has mountains, hills, lakes,
rivers and green landscapes. Fact two, the capital city is Jutega. Jutega is the
political capital of Burundi. It is located in the central part of the country. The city
is an important center for government and culture. Bujambura is the largest city and
an important economic center. Many people live and work in Bujambura. Fact three, Burundi
has two official languages. Kirundi and French are official languages. Kirundi is spoken
by most people in the country. English is also an official language. People may use different
languages at school, at work and in daily life. Language is an important part of Burundi
and culture. Fact four, Burundi has a long history. People have lived in this region for
many centuries. The Kingdom of Burundi was an important part of the country's history.
The country later became part of German East Africa. After the First World War, it was administered
by Belgium. Burundi became independent in 1962. Fact five, Burundi is a very green country.
Burundi has many green hills and valleys. The climate is generally warm. Rain helps plants
and crops grow. The countryside can look especially beautiful during the rainy season. Many people
enjoy the natural beauty of the country. Fact six, Burundi has Lake Tanganyika. Lake Tanganyika
is one of the largest and deepest lakes in the world. It is located along the western side
of Burundi. The lake is shared by several countries. People use the lake for fishing and transportation.
The beaches around the lake are also popular places to relax. Fact seven, Burundi has beautiful
mountains and hills. Burundi is sometimes called the land of a thousand hills. The country has
many hills and highland areas. The scenery can be very beautiful. People farm on many of
the hills. Visitors can enjoy wonderful views of the countryside. Fact eight, agriculture
is very important. Many people in Burundi work in agriculture. Farmers grow crops such
as coffee, tea, bananas, beans, maize and cassava. Farming provides food and income for many
families. Coffee and tea are also important products for the country. The countryside is
full of farms and gardens. Fact nine, Burundi is famous for coffee. Coffee is one of Burundi's
important exports. The country has highland areas that are good for growing coffee. Many
farmers grow coffee on small farms. Burundi and coffee is known in different parts of the world.
Coffee is an important part of the country's economy. Fact ten, tea is also important. Burundi
has many tea growing areas. Tea grows well in the country's highlands. Farmers collect tea
leaves and send them for processing. Tea is another important agricultural product. The
green tea fields are beautiful to see. Fact eleven, family is very important. Family is
an important part of Burundian life. People often spend time with parents, grandparents
and relatives. Children learn traditions from older family members. Families help each other
in daily life. Respect for older people is important. Fact twelve, Burundi has famous
traditional drummers. Drumming is an important part of Burundian culture. The royal drummers
of Burundi are famous around the world. The drummers perform with large traditional drums. Their
performances include rhythm, movement and dance. Traditional drumming is an important symbol
of Burundi. Act thirteen, traditional dancing is popular. Music and dancing are important
during celebrations. People dance at festivals, weddings and other special events. Traditional
dances can include colorful clothing and energetic movements. Dance helps people celebrate their
culture. It is also a way to pass traditions to younger generations. Fact fourteen, football
is very popular. Many people in Burundi enjoy football. Children often play football with
friends. People watch important matches together. The national team represents Burundi in international
competitions. Football brings communities together. Fact fifteen, Burundi has many birds
and animals. The country has forests, wetlands, mountains and lakes. These natural areas provide
homes for many animals. Visitors can see different kinds of birds. There are also monkeys, antelopes
and other wildlife. Protecting nature is important for the future. Fact sixteen, Burundi has beautiful
national parks. Burundi has several protected natural areas. Kabira National Park is one
of the country's important forests. The park has many trees, plants, birds and animals. It
is an important place for nature and wildlife. Visitors can explore some areas with local
guides. Fact seventeen, Burundi has colorful markets. Markets are important places in many
Burundian communities. People buy vegetables, fruit, clothes and handmade products. Markets
can be busy and colorful. Farmers often bring their products to sell. Markets are also
places where people meet and talk. Fact eighteen, Burundi has traditional crafts. Local artists
make many handmade products. These can include baskets, pottery, fabrics and wooden objects.
Many crafts are made by hand using local materials. Traditional skills are passed from parents to
children. Crafts are an important part of Burundian culture. Fact nineteen, Hospitality is important.
Burundian people often welcome guests warmly. Sharing food and conversation is an important
part of social life. Visitors can learn about local traditions by meeting local people.
Family, friendship and community are important values. Hospitality helps visitors feel welcome.
Fact twenty, Burundi is a country full of nature and culture. It has green hills,
beautiful lakes, coffee and tea farms, traditional music, dancing and rich history.
The country may be small, but it has many interesting places to discover.
Burundi is a special country with beautiful landscapes and strong traditions.
Keep listening, keep practicing and keep enjoying English.
